title.narrative: Empowering Women Entrepreneurs and Upgrading MSMEs for Economic Transformation and Jobs in DRC Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Empowering Women Entrepreneurs and Upgrading Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) for Economic Transformation and Jobs in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Project for Congo, Democratic Republic of is to enhance growth of new and existing MSMEs, especially women-owned, and promote job creation particularly for women in select geographic areas. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Support women entrepreneurs, firm creation, and Small And Medium Enterprises (SMEs) upgrading, has the following sub-components: (i) Support professionalization of women entrepreneurs; (ii) Training and competitive grants for creating new firms; and (iii) Matching grants for SMEs upgrading. 2) The second component, Financial inclusion and sustainable access to finance for women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, has the following sub-components: (i) Strengthen credit infrastructure; (ii) Unlock financing for women entrepreneurs; and (iii) Lower the cost and risk of digital financial services. 3) The third component, Entrepreneurship ecosystem development, has the following sub-components: (i) Business environment reforms to catalyze investment; (ii) Institutional capacity development for private sector reforms; (iii) Shared infrastructure and market access. 4) The fourth component, Project implementation, will finance activities related to project management, coordination, communication, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and possible scaling up of activities to additional geographic locations. 5) The fifth component, Contingency Emergency Response Component, will allow for rapid reallocation of uncommitted funds in the event of an eligible emergency.
The project development objective is to enhance growth of new and existing MSMEs, especially women-owned, and promote job creation particularly for women in select geographic areas.

comment.narrative: This indicator intends to count the total number of full time-jobs the project contributed to creating. title.narrative: Public agencies offer new/improved programs and services to support entrepreneurs, MSMEs and private investors in the DRC

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the effect of the institutional capacity building of various public sector agencies involved in investment promotion and entrepreneurship development, including the investment promotion agency, the newly created agency for enterprises development, the National Agency for the Environment, national laboratories, certification centers, and other public facilities, and social public procurement.

title.narrative: Firms benefiting from private sector initiatives
Implemented reforms supporting private sector development
Public agencies offer new/improved programs and services to support entrepreneurs, MSMEs and private investors in the DRC

comment.narrative: The Project has supported a program for the creation, registration, and formalization of businesses within the One-Stop Shop for Business Creation (GUCE). Between April and May, mobile registration/formalization sessions took place in Kananga and Mbuji-Mayi, benefiting 1,366 businesses (Kananga: 613 (468 registered + 145 formalized businesses) / Mbuji-Mayi: 753 (295 registered + 458 formalized)). The Project launched three programs to support the Ministry of Justice, including: i) digitization of commercial courts, ii) revitalization of GUCE by building its capacity, and iii) activating the law on the notary profession.

title.narrative: Number of MSMEs supported with grants

comment.narrative: A total of 1,869 women micro-entrepreneurs who had benefited from training under the previous PADMPME project received a grant under the current TRANSFORME project.

title.narrative: Productive infrastructure investments supported by the project that apply climate resilience standards

comment.narrative: The Project organized environmental training sessions for financial institutions in May 2024. New results will be available once the supported business plans of Component 1 begin to be implemented. Surveys of end beneficiaries of Component 2 are also planned, which will provide additional data for this indicator.

title.narrative: Productive infrastructure investments supported by the project that apply climate resilience standards

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the overall funding portfolio dedicated to climate mitigation or adaptation activities, such as clean energy investments, climate change capacity training plan, adaptation plan, waste management, and recycling. This funding will be primarily allocated under the subsidies (in-kind grants to women entrepreneurs, grants for new MSMEs, matching grants for existing SMEs, and subsidies to SME Centers).

title.narrative: Implemented reforms supporting private sector development

comment.narrative: Special Economic Zone Reform: The Project supported the development of seven draft decrees, three of which have already been published. A decree was also published for the Reform of the Digitalization of Commercial Justice Procedures.
The number of jobs created by each of the 211 women micro-entrepreneurs ranged between 1 and 5.

title.narrative: Additional jobs created by supported MSMEs

comment.narrative: The supported women micro-entrepreneurs have created 284 direct jobs so far, including 172 in the service sector, 98 in agro-processing, and 14 in light industry.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of entrepreneurship and management support (technical and behavioral training and mentoring)

comment.narrative: A total of 30,454 participants were trained in the Personal Initiative Training (21,519 participants) and in the Entrepreneurship Promotion Training (8,935 participants) in the cities of Bunia (6,039), Mbuji-Mayi (6,121), Kananga (6,576), Kinshasa (7,699) and Matadi (4,019). Training in Bukavu and Goma has been suspended due to the security situation in the East.
The indicator measures the number of persons benefited from financial services in operations supported by the Bank, and the number of businesses that benefited from financial services.

title.narrative: Guaranteed loans disbursed to MSMEs with support of the Partial Portfolio Credit Guarantee fund

comment.narrative: Amount of loans disbursed to MSMEs that are backed up by the Portfolio Credit Guarantee fund
A total of 4,498 MSMEs benefited from financial services through loans facilitated by the Partial Credit Guarantee Fund.

title.narrative: Guaranteed loans disbursed to MSMEs with support of the Partial Portfolio Credit Guarantee fund

comment.narrative: The 4,498 MSMEs benefited from US$ 57,421,323 in loans facilitated by the Partial Credit Guarantee Fund. A total of 1,044 loans were granted to young people (18-35 years old), equivalent to US$ 9,413,186.
Remaining available PPCGF endowment for the MSMEs as percentage of the endowment received.

The Partial Credit Guarantee Fund has received all four tranches of its endowment (US$35,037,541), and the total endowment currently stands at US$35,037,559. The endowment is expected to increase based on the integration, after certification of the accounts, of interest generated by term deposits made with certain financial institutions. At the same time, collateral called and paid amounted to approximately US$ 90,500, bringing the deterioration rate to 0.29% for the entire portfolio. The deterioration of the security situation in the East raises concerns about the future evolution of the overall quality of the portfolio.
